prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2005 – Summary (under 500 words)

Core values: Freedom, Fairness, Trust, with a “green thread” across all policies and strong internationalism.

How it’s paid for:
- Redirect around £5bn/year from low-priority spend: abolish the DTI and subsidies; scrap ID cards; redirect the Child Trust Fund to schools.
- One net tax rise: 50% rate only on income over £100,000 to fund three pledges: abolish student tuition/top-up fees; free personal care for elderly/disabled; cut and replace Council Tax with a fairer Local Income Tax (typical household saves ~£450).

Health:
- Free personal care (as in Scotland); faster diagnosis using all available capacity; more scans out of hours; publish test waiting times.
- Free eye/dental checks; extend prescription charge exemptions; more GPs, nurses, therapists; end Whitehall targets and red tape.
- Reform NHS dentistry; Personal Care Plans for long-term conditions; more hospice/palliative care; end age discrimination; ban smoking in enclosed public places; raise school meal standards and restrict junk-food ads to children.

Education and skills:
- Abolish tuition and top-up fees; restore fair grants.
- Cut infant class sizes to average 20 and juniors to 25 using Child Trust Fund money; extend 8am–6pm provision; 3,500 Children’s Centres by 2010.
- Ensure qualified teachers in core subjects; reduce high-stakes testing at 7 and 11; tackle behaviour; boost SEN support.
- 14–19 diplomas blending academic and vocational routes; equal funding for equivalent courses; invest in colleges; protect free school transport distances.
- Green every school/college/university build.

Crime, liberty, immigration:
- 10,000 extra police by scrapping ID cards; cut police bureaucracy; focus on traffickers/serious drug crime.
- Tough community sentences making offenders pay back; targeted action on binge drinking/late-night policing.
- Prison focus on literacy, skills and work; create a UK Border Force.
- Repeal flawed control-order regime; prosecute terror in normal courts (allow intercept evidence); defend jury trial.
- Single Equality Act; create hate-crime units; fair, faster asylum via a dedicated agency and allow asylum seekers to work.

Economy and business:
- Keep fiscal rules; NAO scrutiny of Budget; make ONS independent; curb irresponsible credit marketing.
- Replace Council Tax with Local Income Tax; raise stamp duty threshold to £150,000; managed economic migration; prepare to join euro when conditions met (referendum).
- Cut red tape with costed tests and sunset clauses; one-stop inspections; small business rates relief; scrap DTI and reinvest; legal duty to trade fairly; boost English tourism.

Pensions and welfare:
- Citizen’s Pension from 75, earnings-linked (at least £109.45 single, £167.05 couple), lifting 1m off means-testing; Local Income Tax helps 8 in 10 pensioners.
- First-child maternity pay at minimum wage (£170/week) for 6 months.
- Replace failing CSA with HMRC-run maintenance; reform New Deal; Winter Fuel Payment for severely disabled; stronger pension protection; cut fraud/error by simplifying benefits.

Communities, housing, services:
- Use public land to build 100,000 affordable homes; favour brownfield via VAT reform; planning control for second homes; protect Post Offices and universal mail; restore Lottery independence; streamline inspections.

Europe and world:
- Opposed Iraq war; support Iraqi transition and aim to withdraw UK troops by end of UN mandate.
- Back UN/EU reform; support EU Constitution with a UK referendum.
- Defence: protect overstretched forces; reform procurement; cut Eurofighter tranche 3; retain minimum nuclear deterrent while pursuing disarmament; tougher arms export oversight.

Environment and transport:
- Carbon Tax replacing Climate Change Levy; at least 20% electricity from renewables by 2020; no new nuclear replacements; climate leadership (contraction and convergence).
- Zero municipal waste goal; 60% recycling within 7 years.
- Rail reform with longer, larger franchises; fund safety and key upgrades.
- Incentivise low-emission cars via VED; expand congestion charging; long-term national road pricing to replace fuel duty/VED.
- Free off-peak buses for pensioners/disabled and free rail discount cards; limit new road building; boost cycling, rail freight, waterways; per-aircraft (not per-passenger) aviation taxes; oppose SE airport expansion.

Better government:
- Curb PM power with a War Powers Act; Civil Service Act; predominantly elected second chamber; STV for Commons and local elections; votes at 16.
- Devolve more to Wales/NI; consider further Scottish powers; shift health planning to elected local authorities; merge inspectorates; move civil service jobs out of London.
- Independent BBC regulator appointed by Parliament; Environmental Responsibility Act; align environment/transport/energy in one department.
